title: Choose the public site composition
question: You asked for a public journal, not an app shell. The starship elbow console was dropped for that reason. The roll assigned Folio with catchwords.

options.label: Folio with catchwords
options.thesis: The public site is one opened folio: the landing is the first leaf, each note hands you to the next with a catchword.
options.viewport: Newsreader statement on the first leaf; two or three notes already visible below, each ending with the next title in quiet type.
options.risk: Catchwords can feel bibliographic if they outrank the note titles.

raised.raise: Hierarchy is scale contrast alone: the landing is the giant first word, notes stay on one measure.
Opening one note does not reshuffle the others; the folio keeps its order.

options.label: Margin chronicle
options.thesis: Dates live in a wide margin; the body is one continuous journal you read down the page.
options.viewport: Left margin of dates, right column: landing standfirst then published notes in the same voice, several already on screen.
options.risk: A wide margin can look like an admin inspector if the dates become metadata chips.

options.label: Running header journal
options.thesis: Site name as a running head; the landing is the first paragraph of a magazine that continues into notes.
options.viewport: Quiet running head, large first paragraph, then article-length notes in the same column with titles in Newsreader.
options.risk: Can collapse into a generic blog if the first paragraph is not clearly the landing record.

options.label: Type specimen
options.thesis: The landing is one enormous Newsreader setting; published notes occupy the specimen grid beneath, hierarchy by scale alone.
options.viewport: A huge landing title filling the first screen’s upper half; notes in a measured grid below, already readable.
options.case: Readers identify a publication immediately; scale does the persuading without an app frame.
options.risk: A foundry demo can outrank the journal if the giant word is the product name instead of the landing statement.

options.label: Merz collage
options.thesis: Notes as pasted scraps with no dominant reading axis.
options.viewport: A pinboard of landing and notes at angles.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a journal needs a reading order, and scraps read as art direction not publication.
options.kept: Opening one note does not reshuffle the folio.
options.risk: Angles, mixed faces, and a pinboard are an app of another kind.

options.label: Teletext magazine
options.thesis: Keyed pages on a character grid.
options.viewport: Page 100 index, notes as numbered pages.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it is an addressable console, the app shell you asked to avoid.
options.kept: Notes remain addressable without becoming an index UI.
options.risk: Black mosaic and keyed pages cannot wear Kernel’s paper journal.
